source.excerpt: It is love alone that gives value to all things.
trail: Wikiquote cites “V: Loving complaints and petitions; Martha’s complaint” in volume 1, page 379.
ICS Publications identifies volume 1 as including the Soliloquies and credits translators Kieran Kavanaugh and Otilio Rodriguez. Its catalog page does not reproduce page 379.
The source is a modern English rendering of Teresa’s writing. The age of the Spanish original does not make this English translation public domain.

author.heading: About Teresa of Ávila
author.bio: Teresa of Ávila (1515–1582) was a Spanish Carmelite reformer and mystical writer. She founded reformed Carmelite communities and wrote The Life, The Way of Perfection and The Interior Castle; her work connects the practice of prayer with the demands of community life.

context.heading: Why it mattered
lead: The cited setting is a soliloquy framed around Martha’s complaint, placing the sentence within Teresa’s language of prayer and love. The English collected volume brings together her autobiography, spiritual testimonies and soliloquies. Because this exact English page has not been inspected, the citation is retained as a sourced attribution rather than a primary-page verification.
